lesson_scope: Extremal modulus and argument values for complex loci: maximum and minimum |z| on circles and lines, maximum and minimum arg(z) via geometric tangents and trigonometry, exact coordinates of extreme points, distance optimization between disjoint circles, and extremal values on bounded regions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Maximum and minimum modulus on a circle locus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Max and min modulus on circle.

hints: Max modulus is $13 + 4 = 17$, min modulus is $13 - 4 = 9$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate distance from origin to centre:
$$|z_0| = |5 + 12\mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{25 + 144} = 13$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Maximum and minimum distance from a circle to an external point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Extremal distance from circle to fixed non-origin point.

hints: Distance from centre $4 + 4\mathrm{i}$ to point $1$ is $|(4+4\mathrm{i}) - 1| = |3 + 4\mathrm{i}| = 5$.
Greatest value is $5 + 2 = 7$, least value is $5 - 2 = 3$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate distance from circle centre to point $w = 1$:
$$|z_0 - 1| = |(4 + 4\mathrm{i}) - 1| = |3 + 4\mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$$

Add and subtract radius $r = 2$:
$$\text{Greatest value} = 5 + 2 = 7$$
$$\text{Least value} = 5 - 2 = 3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains greatest value $7$ and least value $3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Minimum modulus on perpendicular bisector through origin.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Minimum modulus on bisector line.

hints: The line passes through the origin $(0, 0)$, so minimum modulus is at $z = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify line equation:
$$|z - 4| = |z - 4\mathrm{i}| \implies (x - 4)^2 + y^2 = x^2 + (y - 4)^2 \implies y = x$$

Locate point of minimum modulus:
$$\text{Since } y = x \text{ passes through } (0, 0), \text{ the minimum modulus point is } z = 0.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies line $y = x$ passes through origin.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Half-angle from tangent geometry on a circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent angle alpha from sine relation.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Maximum and minimum argument on circle locus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding max and min argument on circle.

hints: Max argument is $\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}$, min argument is $\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\pi}{6} = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate centre argument and tangent angle:
$$\arg(z_0) = \arctan\left(\frac{2}{2\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}, \quad |z_0| = 4$$
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{r}{|z_0|} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \alpha = \frac{\pi}{6}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Point of maximum modulus on circle locus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding exact coordinates of max modulus point on circle.

hints: Centre is $3 + 4\mathrm{i}$ with $|z_0| = 5$, and radius is $2$.
Max modulus is $7$, scale centre by $\frac{7}{5}$: $\frac{7}{5}(3 + 4\mathrm{i}) = \frac{21}{5} + \frac{28}{5}\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine scale factor for maximum modulus:
$$|z_0| = 5, \quad |z|_{\max} = 5 + 2 = 7 \implies \text{Scale factor } = \frac{7}{5}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Minimum modulus point on a perpendicular bisector.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving linear bisector equation.
Finding point of least modulus on perpendicular bisector.

walkthrough.text:
Minimise squared modulus along the line $x = 2y - 4$:
$$|z|^2 = (2y - 4)^2 + y^2 = 5y^2 - 16y + 16$$
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}y}(|z|^2) = 10y - 16 = 0 \implies y = \frac{8}{5}, \quad x = 2\left(\frac{8}{5}\right) - 4 = -\frac{4}{5}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Minimises $x^2 + y^2$ (or uses perpendicular distance formula).

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Trigonometric analysis of maximum argument.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding centre distance and sine of tangent angle.

hints: Tangent triangle has opposite $2$ and hypotenuse $5$, so $\sin\alpha = \frac{2}{5}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up right-angled triangle with opposite $2$ and hypotenuse $5$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Evaluating maximum argument to 3 decimal places.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Exact Cartesian coordinates of tangent contact point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Tangent length and exact trig ratios.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate tangent length from origin:
$$L = \sqrt{|z_0|^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{100 - 25} = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$$

Determine exact sine and cosine of half-angle $\alpha$:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{10} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \alpha = \frac{\pi}{6}, \quad \cos\alpha = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding exact Cartesian coordinates of tangent point using compound angles.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Extremal values on a bounded circular segment.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding max real part and max modulus on bounded disk.

walkthrough.text:
Find point of maximum real part:
$$x_{\max} = 5 + 3 = 8 \implies (8, 2) \text{ or } 8 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies point of maximum real part as $(8, 2)$.
Identifies maximum modulus occurs on outer boundary where $x > 5$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding maximum argument on region where tangent lies outside domain.

hints: Check tangent point: $x$-coordinate is less than $5$, so tangent contact point is outside the region.
Max argument occurs at corner vertex $(5, 5)$.

walkthrough.text:
Check if circle tangent contact point satisfies $x \geqslant 5$:
$$\text{The tangent from origin has } x_T < 5, \text{ which lies outside the domain } x \geqslant 5.$$

Evaluate argument at top vertex $(5, 5)$:
$$\arg(5 + 5\mathrm{i}) = \arctan\left(\frac{5}{5}\right) = \frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785 \text{ rad}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Notes that circle tangent contact point has $x < 5$.
Tests boundary vertices and identifies $(5, 5)$ as extremal point.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Full algebraic and geometric determination of extreme modulus and argument.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding max/min modulus values and exact coordinates.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate exact coordinates of extreme points along ray through centre:
$$z_{\max} = \frac{7}{5}(3 + 4\mathrm{i}) = \frac{21}{5} + \frac{28}{5}\mathrm{i} = (4.2, 5.6)$$
$$z_{\min} = \frac{3}{5}(3 + 4\mathrm{i}) = \frac{9}{5} + \frac{12}{5}\mathrm{i} = (1.8, 2.4)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating max and min argument to 3 decimal places.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Distance optimization between two moving points on disjoint circles.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Distance between centres and min/max distance between circles.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate minimum and maximum distances between circles:
$$|z - w|_{\min} = D - (r_1 + r_2) = 10 - (2 + 3) = 5$$
$$|z - w|_{\max} = D + (r_1 + r_2) = 10 + (2 + 3) = 15$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding exact points achieving minimum distance between circles.

hints: Unit vector along line of centres is $\hat{u} = \frac{6+8\mathrm{i}}{10} = \frac{3}{5} + \frac{4}{5}\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate unit vector along line of centres:
$$\hat{u} = \frac{z_2 - z_1}{D} = \frac{6 + 8\mathrm{i}}{10} = \frac{3}{5} + \frac{4}{5}\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Special circle with vertical tangent giving maximum argument pi/2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Modulus and argument of circle centre.
Finding exact max and min arguments.
Finding exact Cartesian form of maximum argument point.

ai_rubric.observable: Recognises $z$ is on positive imaginary axis ($x = 0$).
